Actor.description: Ignored since 1.1: the audit actor and `provenance.agent` are the authenticated principal.
Actor.name: x-memhouse-actor

IdempotencyKey.description: 1 to 255 characters. A repeat with the same key and request returns the first response; the same key with another request is a 409. Same as the body's `request_key`.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

User.description: The user the call acts for. Accepted only from admins and from agents trusted to act for users (`act_as`); a user's key always acts for that user, a token for its own user.
User.name: x-memhouse-user

Admission.description: How proposals from agents without a commit grant are admitted (GOV-08).

oneOf.description: The engine commits a proposal as soon as it passes the write gate.

Proposals stay `candidate` until a principal with `memory:review` commits or rejects them.
Conversation rounds (`ingest`) are always admitted by the engine.

CodeRef.description: A file a memory is about (TR-TPL-02): stale when the file's content hash changes.

CompiledPolicy.description: A compiled policy and the version records and traces are stamped with.

version.description:
`gov-<hash>` for the default policy, `policy-v<n>-<hash>` for an approved spec,
`draft-<hash>` for one only validated. The hash is of the body, so equal policies get
equal versions on every node.

CompiledPolicyBody.description: Everything a policy decides, with nothing left unset: the body stored in `mh_policy`.

decisions.description: Access-decision values (D-01…D-07), from the decision register in G28.

spec.description: The spec it was compiled from; absent for the default policy (the configuration).

oldest_pending_secs.description: Age of the oldest pending job, in seconds (queue lag).

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

error.description: What went wrong, for people. The wording may change between releases.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error codes. Clients branch on these, never on the message text.

oneOf.description: The request is malformed or fails validation (400).
Missing or wrong API key (401).
The caller is known but may not do this (403).
The record (or route) doesn't exist (404).

The request conflicts with the stored state: an idempotency key reused for another
request, or a revision of a record that is no longer the current version (409).
A failure inside MemHouse or its database or models (500).

A dependency is down for now (the intake queue, the database): retry later (503, with
`Retry-After`). Nothing was written (PERF-07).

ExactQuery.description: An exact structured-record query inside a recall (HYB-02, HYB-03).

attrs.description: A JSON object the record's attributes must contain (`{"order_id": "A-1001"}`).

record_type.description: Only records of this type (`order`, `address`, ...); any type when absent.

ExcludedRecord.description: A record left out of a recall, and why.

detail.description: Identifiers and values only, never content (e.g. `label hr`, `valid_to 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`).

ExclusionReason.description: Why a record that matched a recall's query is not among its results (GOV-04).

oneOf.description: Not recallable in its state: quarantined, candidate, rejected, expired, or superseded.
Scoped to another user, agent, team or org than the caller.
Carries a label denied to the caller.

Not valid at the recall's time: before `valid_from`, after `valid_to` or `expires_at`, or
happened after `as_of`.
Outside the request's own filters: kinds, tags or time window.
Cut by the token budget.
Ranked below the `k` returned.

ForgetRequest.description:
Delete memories (`forget`, CORE-05). Name exactly one of `id`, `subject`, `user`, `agent`,
`source` or `all`. Deletion is permanent and includes every derived representation.

agent.description: Records written by the agent or scoped to it, in any subject.

all.description: The whole tenant. Needs `confirm` set to the tenant's name.

confirm.description: The tenant's name, when `all` is set.

dry_run.description: Count what would be deleted, delete nothing.

id.description: One record (and the facts derived from it).

request_key.description: Idempotency key: a repeat returns the first result instead of `not_found`.

source.description: Records with this source label, in any subject.

subject.description: Everything held about a subject (right to erasure).

user.description: Records the user wrote through an agent or that are scoped to the user, in any subject.

deleted.description:
Records deleted (or, with `dry_run`, that would be). Facts derived from them are deleted
too and are not counted unless they match themselves.

value.description: The id, subject, user, agent, source or tenant named.

exact.description: Found by an exact structured-record match (HYB-02), not by similarity.

score.description: Fused score; compare it only within one response.

similarity.description: Cosine similarity of the best vector.

IngestRequest.description: Store a conversation as episodic memory, one record per user/assistant round.

per_message.description:
Store every message as its own record instead of grouping user/assistant rounds
(use for multi-party conversations without a "user" role).

session_id.description: Groups the rounds; also the unit of background enrichment. Defaults to a new id.

session_time.description: Session start time; used for messages without their own timestamp.

wait.description: Wait until the rounds are stored, as for `remember`.

ids.description: Ids of the rounds stored (or queued).

queued.description:
True while the rounds are still in the intake queue (the request did not set `wait`):
their ids resolve to `candidate` until the pipeline has stored them.

stored.description: Rounds stored; while `queued`, the rounds accepted into the intake queue.

expires_at.description: After this the record is no longer recalled (working memory, MEM-01).

occurred_at.description: When the remembered thing happened (event time), if known.

source.description: Source label: the writer by default, `enrich:<model>` for extracted facts.

status.description: Lifecycle state; only `committed` records are recalled.

supersedes.description: The previous version, which this record replaced.

valid_to.description: When it stopped being true; set when it is superseded.

oneOf.description: Short-lived task context for one session; expires (MEM-01).
Raw conversation history: a user/assistant round.
Durable facts about the subject.
Likes, dislikes, ways of working.
How-to knowledge, conventions, procedures.
Promises, follow-ups, open items with a due date.
Reference documents or snippets.

MemoryPage.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is absent on the
last page. Cursors are opaque.

MemoryStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a record (CORE-02). Only `committed` records are recalled.

```text
candidate ──► committed ──► superseded
    │  │          │  └────► expired
    │  └► rejected │
    └──► quarantined ◄┘ ──► rejected   (quarantined ──► committed on release)
```

oneOf.description: Proposed, waiting for its gate (asynchronous admission, G10).
Replaced by a newer version (`superseded_by`).
Held back by the gate (for example an injected instruction).
Refused by the gate or a reviewer.
Past `expires_at` (working memory, commitments).

Message.description: One message of a conversation handed to `ingest`.

id.description: Caller's own reference for the message (for provenance and evaluation).

role.description: `user`, `assistant`, or a participant's name in a multi-party conversation.

timestamp.description: When the message was sent; defaults to the request's `session_time`.

PolicyActivation.description: One activation: what ran from then on.

compiled.description: The compiled policy version records were stamped with from then on.

version.description: The spec version activated; absent for the default policy.

PolicyChange.description: One changed setting between two compiled policies.

PolicyDiff.description: The settings that differ between two compiled policies.

from.description: `default` or a version (`3`, `v3`); absent: the policy running now.

spec.description: A spec to compare, compiled but not stored.

to.description: `default` or a version; give this or `spec`.

PolicySpec.description:
A behaviour policy as authored (TOML or JSON). Every section and field is optional: what a spec
leaves out keeps the governance or configured value.

name.description: A short name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

allowed.description: Kinds that may be written; writes of other kinds are refused. Default: all.

PolicySpecRanking.description: Ranking weights (the meaning of each is in `[memory]` of the configuration reference).

audit_reads.description: Audit every recall; can't be turned off where governance turns it on.

denied_labels.description: Labels never read; must include every label governance denies.

categories.description: Categories redacted before anything is stored; must include every governance category.

PolicySpecRef.description: The approved spec a compiled policy came from.

version.description: The spec's version number; absent for a draft that was only validated.

note.description: Why the change is proposed (kept with the version).

episodic_days.description:
Days after which episodic memory is purged; 0 keeps it. Where governance purges, at most
its days and never 0.

working_ttl_secs.description: Lifetime of working memory written without `expires_at` (1 second to 30 days).

PolicySpecScope.description: What the policy governs. v1: one tenant (layers by org, team and agent come in G24).

oneOf.description: Stored, not yet approved: it never executes.
Approved by a named approver; may be activated (and rolled back to).

admission.description: `auto` or `review`; `auto` only where governance doesn't require review.

dedup_threshold.description: Cosine similarity at which a new memory counts as a duplicate (0.5 to 1).

quarantine_injection.description: Always on (security baseline); may be stated, never turned off.

PolicyStatus.description: The active policy of a tenant, its spec versions and its activations.

active.description: The spec version activated last; absent while the default policy runs.

running.description: The compiled policy that runs now.

warning.description:
Set when the active spec no longer compiles under the current governance, so the default
policy runs instead.

PolicyValidation.description: Whether a spec compiles for the caller's tenant, and to what.

PolicyViolation.description: A setting that doesn't compile, and why.

Provenance.description:
Who and what admitted a record (GOV-03), and which model derived it (TR-MS-02). The source
turn is the record's `session_id` and `turn_ref`; its confidence is `confidence`.

extractor.description: For derived records: the model that extracted it, and its prompt and configuration.

policy_version.description: The compiled policy that admitted the record (`mh_policy`; `legacy-v1` before schema v2).

request_key.description: The client's idempotency key for the request that wrote it (CORE-06).

user.description: The user the agent acted for, when known.

exact.description:
Identifiers in the question ("A-1001", "#4521") looked up exactly in structured records
(HYB-03): the plan then mixes keyword, vector and exact retrieval.

RecallExplanation.description:
A recall's explanation (`GET /v1/recalls/{id}/explanation`, GOV-04): what it returned and why,
and the records that matched the query but were left out, each with its reason. Exclusions for
access, labels and state are recomputed from the store when the explanation is read
(`replayed_at`); budget and rank cuts are as recorded.

excluded.description: Most relevant first, by reason order (status, access, label, validity, filter, budget, rank).

hidden.description:
Excluded records this viewer may not know about, counted by reason (ids are shown only to
principals with `audit:read`).

RecallRecord.description: What a recall was asked, how it was authorized and what it returned, kept for its explanation.

authorizer.description: The authorizer that decided (`scope`; `rebac` from G27).

cut.description: Records the recall itself cut (budget, rank); the explanation adds the rest.

scope.description: The scope filter applied (the caller's own, merged with the request's).

valid_at.description: The time validity was checked at.

RecallRequest.description: Retrieve memories for a context (`recall`, CORE-03).

analyze.description: Override query analysis (time windows and sub-queries) on/off.

as_of.description: Recall what was true at this time (validity and event-time filter).

exact.description:
An exact query over structured records (HYB-02): records of this type whose attributes
contain these values are returned first, matched exactly, never by similarity.

include_candidates.description:
Also return candidates (plans and speculation the gate holds, proposals waiting for
review), each labelled by its `status` (PR-7). Default recall never returns them.

k.description: Number of memories to return (default `memory.default_k`, at most 200).

query.description: What you need to know, in natural language.

reference_time.description:
"Now" for reading relative time in the query ("two weeks ago"). Defaults to `as_of`, then
the current time. Unlike `as_of` it filters nothing.

render.description: Also return the memories as a text block ready for a prompt (`rendered`, INT-04).

scope.description:
Only memories visible in this scope: each scope field the request sets matches records
with the same value or none. Unset fields don't filter.

subject.description: Whose memory to search. Recall never crosses subjects.

tags.description: Only memories with at least one of these tags.

token_budget.description: Approximate token budget for the returned memories.

degraded.description:
Set when retrieval failed or ran out of time: `hits` is then empty, not a real answer
(PERF-07). The value says why; callers should go on without memory, not retry in a loop.

embed_ms.description: Time spent embedding the query, in the SQL statement, and reranking.

hits.description: Ranked memories, most relevant first, each with its id and provenance.

plan.description: How the query was read: time windows and sub-queries that got their own retrieval probe.

recall_id.description: Id of this recall's explanation (`GET /v1/recalls/{id}/explanation`, GOV-04).

rendered.description: The hits as a model-neutral text block, when the request set `render`.

RecallStages.description: Time spent per stage of a recall.

instrument_ms.description:
Time the recall spent on its own instrumentation: metrics and this record (the row itself is
written off the request path).

probes.description: Probes run in that statement: the query, plus a time window or sub-queries it mentions.

statements.description: Database round trips on the synchronous path (PERF-02).

RelabelRequest.description:
Replace a record's sensitivity labels (`POST /v1/labels`, ACC-04). No new version and no
re-embedding.

labels.description: The complete new set of labels.

actor.description:
Who makes the change, for the audit log; defaults to the `x-memhouse-actor` header. From
API keys per principal (G06) the authenticated principal is used instead.

code_refs.description: Files the memory is about, for staleness checks.

content.description: The memory, written so it stands alone (who, what, when), ideally one fact.

expires_at.description: When it stops being recalled; `working` memory defaults to now + `memory.working_ttl_secs`.

labels.description: Sensitivity labels (ACC-04); `governance.denied_labels` keeps them out of recall.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object, stored as given.

occurred_at.description: When the remembered thing happened; defaults to now.

request_key.description:
Idempotency key (or the `Idempotency-Key` header): a repeat with the same key and request
returns the first result; the same key with another request is a conflict (CORE-06).

source.description: Source label; defaults to the actor.

structured.description: The queryable form of the record (an order, a ticket), under the same id.

subject.description: Whose memory it is, e.g. `user:alice`, `customer:42`, `repo:api`. Defaults to the configured subject.

supersedes.description: Replace an existing memory with this one; prefer `revise`.

tags.description: Free tags, usable as recall filters.

tenant.description: The tenant; defaults to the configured one.

user.description: The user the calling agent acts for (provenance).

valid_to.description: When it stops being true (a due date, an expiry).

wait.description:
Wait for the write gate before answering (at most `intake.wait_timeout_ms`): the result
then carries the record's final state. By default `remember` answers as soon as the
redacted write is durably queued, with `status: candidate` (CORE-02).

RememberResult.description:
What a write did. The id is returned at once; `status` says the record's state, which can
also be read later with `GET /v1/memories/{id}` (CORE-02).

deduplicated.description: True when an equivalent memory already existed and nothing new was written.

id.description: The record's id. For a deduplicated write, the id of the memory already stored.

note.description: Why the write was deduplicated, held, quarantined or rejected.

redactions.description: Kinds of sensitive data redacted from the text (`card`, `secret`, ...).

route.description: The representation the record was routed to (HYB-01), once the gate has run.

statement.description: What the gate read the statement as (QUAL-02), once it has run.

status.description:
`candidate` while the write waits for the gate (the default answer); with `wait`, the
gate's decision: `committed`, `candidate` (a plan or speculation held until confirmed, or a
proposal waiting for review), `quarantined` or `rejected`. Clients must not assume a write
is committed: read `GET /v1/memories/{id}` for its state.

ReturnedRecord.description: A record a recall returned, with its ranking signals.

ReviewRequest.description: Commit or reject a candidate (`POST /v1/review`, GOV-08, GOV-11).

reason.description: Why, for the audit log (a rejection's reason).

status.description: `committed`, or `rejected` (also when a revision's predecessor is no longer current).

ReviseRequest.description:
Correct a memory (`revise`, CORE-04): a new version that supersedes the current one. Fields
left out are taken from the current version (kind, tags, labels, scope, metadata, validity,
structured form, code references).

id.description: The memory to revise; it must be the current (`committed`) version.

wait.description: Wait for the write gate, as for `remember`.

to.description: `default` or an approved version; absent: the policy active before the current one.

Route.description: The representation intake routes a record to (HYB-01).

oneOf.description: Conversation or longer prose: text with keyword and vector search.
One self-contained statement: text search plus correction and duplicate checks.

A record with attributes (an order, an address): also a row in the structured table,
answered by exact query (HYB-02).
A statement relating people or organisations; stored as a fact until the graph (G35).

Source code or a change to it; stored as text with the `code` tag until code-aware
memory (G19).

Scope.description:
Narrower visibility inside a subject (MEM-04). All empty means the whole subject; resolution
order (user over team over org) is applied by recall from G11.

Statement.description:
What a statement asserts, as the write gate reads it (QUAL-02). Plans and speculation stay
candidates until confirmed or expired (PR-7); a correction supersedes what it corrects.

oneOf.description: Something true now ("Acme's renewal date is 1 March").
Something that happened ("The user adopted a cat in March").
A change to, or fix of, something stored before ("Actually, she moved to Porto").
An intention not yet carried out ("The user plans to visit Japan in May").
A guess, rumour or hypothetical ("He might switch vendors").
A like, dislike or way of working.
How something should be done ("Run the tests before every commit").

Structured.description: The queryable form of a structured record (HYB-02), under the same id as its text.

attrs.description: A JSON object of attributes, queried exactly, never by similarity.

SubjectCount.description: A subject and its number of committed memories.

meaning.description: What the phrase resolves to, for people and answer models ("2023-04-15 (Sat)").

phrase.description: The phrase the window was read from.

TokenRequest.description: Ask for a short-lived agent token (`POST /v1/tokens`, GOV-13).

agent.description:
The agent principal the token acts as. Required when a user or an admin asks; an agent
gets a token for itself.

scopes.description: Narrower permissions than the caller's; defaults to all the caller may pass on.

ttl_secs.description: At most `access.token_ttl_secs` (default and maximum 900 unless configured, never above 3600).

user.description:
The user the token acts for. A user's token always acts for that user; an admin or an
agent trusted to act for users (`act_as`) may name one.

agent.description: The agent principal the token acts as.

user.description: The user it acts for, if any.
The verified user the calls act for.

bearer.description: `Authorization: Bearer <key or token>`: a principal's API key (`mh_…`, from `memhouse key create`), a short-lived agent token (`mht.…`, from `POST /v1/tokens`), or a bootstrap key from `[server] api_keys`.

For the principal that recalled, or any principal with `audit:read`; others get 404. Records excluded for status, access or labels are listed by id only to `audit:read`, otherwise counted in `hidden`. The id is `recall_id` of the recall's response.

post.description: Redacts the write, queues it durably and answers at once with the record's id as `candidate` (1.4); the rest of the pipeline (injection screen, statement gate, routing, embedding, deduplication) then runs in the background and the record becomes `committed`, `quarantined` or `rejected`, or stays `candidate` (a plan or a guess). Read the state with `GET /v1/memories/{id}`, or send `wait: true` to answer with the gate's decision. A `503` means nothing was queued: retry with the same idempotency key.
